description: Hi i’m Elis and I’m high school student in Antalya.
summary:
Our project aims to make space exploration more engaging and accessible through an educational video and a story-based interactive children’s book.

Although primarily designed for children aged 8–12, we believe our project can appeal to learners of all ages. We explore the stories of space missions and the spacecraft and objects left behind, following their chronological journeys and discovering their purposes and contributions.

Rather than simply presenting historical facts, we approach space exploration as a mystery waiting to be solved. By following the traces and remnants left behind in space, we revisit past missions, uncover forgotten stories, and encourage children to become little space detectives. This turns learning into an exciting journey of discovery.

Our main goal was to create an entertaining documentary rather than a traditional educational presentation. To make it more interactive, we brought together three speakers and a child listener, creating a natural and engaging conversation that helps young audiences feel part of the story.

The experience continues beyond the video with educational games and stories designed to reinforce learning and encourage curiosity.

Ultimately, we hope to show that even the smallest traces left behind in space can reveal remarkable stories about humanity’s journey beyond Earth.
details:
The main purpose of our project is to offer children an enjoyable and lasting learning experience. We aim to achieve this through a combination of songs, games, storytelling, and an educational documentary, making learning feel less like a lesson and more like an adventure.

One of the strongest aspects of our project is the way we approach our young audience. Instead of overwhelming children with information or making the documentary feel like a traditional lecture, we wanted to create a natural, relatable, and engaging atmosphere. Our curious young listener plays an important role in achieving this. Their questions, imagination, and unique way of thinking reflect how children naturally explore the world. Rather than simply listening to the speakers, children can see their own curiosity and thoughts represented in the video. We believe this connection helps them feel closer to both the story and the information being shared.

We also wanted to give imagination a special place in scientific learning. Science is based on facts, but curiosity is often what inspires us to explore those facts in the first place. While our young listener wants to understand the mysteries of space, they also want to imagine what these mysterious journeys might feel like. Therefore, we tried to take our audience on an adventure where scientific discoveries meet imagination. By following the traces and remains left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond, we explored space as if we were solving a mystery together.

Before starting the project, our team tried to go back five years and think like our younger selves. We asked ourselves three questions: Why did we find certain stories interesting? What were we curious about when it came to space? And what made learning truly fun? These questions became the foundation of our approach and helped us design a project that we ourselves would have enjoyed as children.

We did not use software development in this project. However, we used artificial intelligence as an assisting tool during video editing and website creation.

Overall, this project was not only about teaching children facts about space; it was about understanding how they think, connecting with their imagination, and making discovery an experience they can enjoy. Creating it was a genuinely enjoyable journey for our team, and we hope watching it will be just as enjoyable for our audience.
